prompt.context: A tire manufacturer in Vietnam, VieTire, has been the only player in that market due to high tariffs on imports. They dominate the tire industry. As it stands, the tariff is 50% of the total cost to produce and ship a tire to Vietnam. Because of the forces of globalization and lower consumer prices, the Vietnamese government decided to lower the tariff by 5% a year for the next ten years. VieTire is very concerned about this change, as it will radically alter the landscape of the industry in Vietnam.
prompt.question: They hire you to assess the situation and advise them on what steps to take.

clarifying_info.q: What are the major costs associated with making a tire for VieTire?
clarifying_info.a: Raw materials comprise about 20% of the cost, labor 40%, and all other costs such as overhead 40%. The average tire costs about $40 to make.

clarifying_info.q: Why is labor such a major cost?
clarifying_info.a: Things are done more manually. Most of the technological advances in the industry have not yet been implemented in Vietnam.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost structure for foreign competitors?
clarifying_info.a: An average tire manufacturer in the US produces tires at a cost of $30 each.

clarifying_info.q: What is the shipping cost to bring a tire to Vietnam?

framework: Understand VieTire's current cost structure (breakdown by raw materials, labor, overhead)
Determine the competitive cost structure of foreign manufacturers
Calculate the landed cost of imported tires under the current tariff
Model how landed cost of imports changes as tariff declines 5% per year
Identify the year foreign competitors become price-competitive with VieTire
Recommend specific operational and strategic steps VieTire can take to protect its position

questions.prompt: What are VieTire's major cost components and how much does it cost to make a tire?
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose VieTire's $40 production cost: raw materials 20% = $8, labor 40% = $16, overhead 40% = $16. Labor at $16 per tire is high because production is manual and technology has not been adopted yet.

math.setup: VieTire cost per tire = $40. Raw materials: 20% x $40. Labor: 40% x $40. Overhead: 40% x $40.
math.answer: Raw materials $8, labor $16, overhead $16; total $40 per tire.

questions.prompt: What is the current landed cost of a US-made imported tire in Vietnam (including shipping and tariff)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should add shipping to US production cost to get base landed cost, then apply the 50% tariff on total cost to produce and ship. Result shows foreign competitors cannot profitably enter today.

math.setup: US production cost = $30, shipping = $4, base landed cost = $34. Tariff = 50% of $34.
math.answer: $51 per tire — more expensive than VieTire's $40, so competitors will not enter.

questions.prompt: Build a year-by-year table: as the tariff drops 5 percentage points per year, when does the imported tire become cheaper than VieTire's $40?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the declining tariff rate to the $34 base cost each year. Strong candidates will note the competition enters the market around year 6 when imported cost falls below $40, with serious consideration beginning in year 4-5.

math.setup: Base landed cost (pre-tariff) = $34. Tariff starts at 50% and falls 5 pp per year. Tariff applies to base landed cost. VieTire domestic cost = $40.
steps: Now: tariff 50%, import cost = $34 x 1.50 = $51.00 — will not enter
Year 1: tariff 45%, import cost = $34 x 1.45 = $49.30 — will not enter
Year 2: tariff 40%, import cost = $34 x 1.40 = $47.60 — will not enter
Year 3: tariff 35%, import cost = $34 x 1.35 = $45.90 — will not enter
Year 4: tariff 30%, import cost = $34 x 1.30 = $44.20 — consideration if willing to cut price
Year 5: tariff 25%, import cost = $34 x 1.25 = $42.50 — preparing to enter
Year 6: tariff 20%, import cost = $34 x 1.20 = $40.80 — entering market
Year 7: tariff 15%, import cost = $34 x 1.15 = $39.10 — competing on price
math.answer: Foreign competitors become cost-competitive around year 6 and enter the market. By year 7 their costs are below VieTire's $40 cost basis. Note: casebook rounds slightly differently (uses $50 base not $34 x 1.50); key insight is year 6 entry.

brainstorming.prompt: What steps can VieTire take to protect itself from increased foreign competition over the next 6 years?

categories.name: Cost Reduction — Operations
ideas: Reengineer production methods to reduce manual labor
Invest in the latest manufacturing technology and automation
Increase worker skills/productivity while containing hourly wages

categories.name: Strategic Positioning
ideas: Develop customer loyalty programs to lock in market share
Build brand equity as the local trusted manufacturer
Pursue long-term supply contracts with large fleet buyers or distributors
Explore government relations to slow or modify tariff schedule

categories.name: Competitive Response
ideas: Lower prices proactively before competitors enter
Pursue volume growth to gain scale advantages
Consider partnerships or joint ventures with foreign tire makers to access technology
Diversify into adjacent markets or higher-margin tire segments

recommendation: VieTire has approximately 4-6 years before foreign competitors meaningfully enter the Vietnamese market
They must urgently reduce production costs — particularly the $16 labor cost — by adopting modern manufacturing technology
Target cost reduction to bring total cost below $34 (the foreign base landed cost) to maintain advantage even as tariffs fall
risks: Technology improvements by foreign competitors could lower their production cost below $30, accelerating market entry beyond year 6
Capital investment in automation is costly and takes time; VieTire may not reduce costs fast enough
Customer loyalty may erode quickly on price if the cost gap narrows
next_steps: Conduct a detailed benchmarking study of US and other global tire manufacturers' production processes
Develop a capital investment plan for technology adoption with a 3-year payback target
Launch a customer loyalty and brand-building program immediately to secure market share before competition arrives
